title: JavaScript Foundations
subtitle: Build interactive browser experiences with data and resilient interface states
intendedFor: Beginners who know basic HTML and want to add behavior, interaction, and local data to web pages.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Complete modules in order. Each module builds language and browser skills needed by the Campus Event Explorer capstone.
courseOverview.summary: A practical beginner JavaScript course covering values, decisions, collections, functions, DOM interaction, events, JSON, promises, async-await, local fetch, resilient interface states, and a complete event explorer.

moduleSummary.title: Values, Variables, and Decisions
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Represent information and make decisions with JavaScript values and expressions.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build a small event announcement generator that responds to changing input data.

moduleSummary.title: Collections, Repetition, and Functions
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Organize event data and reusable behavior with arrays, objects, loops, and functions.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build a reusable event list planner from structured in-memory data.

moduleSummary.title: Browser Interaction and Asynchronous Data
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Render interactive browser interfaces and load local JSON data asynchronously.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build an interactive event browser with explicit loading, error, empty, and success states.

moduleSummary.title: Final Capstone: Campus Event Explorer
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Combine JavaScript fundamentals, browser events, local data loading, and resilient UI states.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build and verify a complete Campus Event Explorer.

modules.title: Values, Variables, and Decisions
modules.purpose: Build a reliable mental model for JavaScript values and use expressions and conditions to turn event information into useful messages.
learningObjectives: Distinguish strings, numbers, booleans, null, and undefined.
Store values with const and let and name them clearly.
Build readable text with string methods and template literals.
Use comparisons, logical operators, and conditionals to choose behavior.
guidedExercises: Inspect values and expressions in small browser-connected examples.
Transform event names, locations, capacities, and availability into messages.
Trace conditional branches before implementing them.
modules.moduleProject: Build an Event Announcement Generator that produces clear messages from event values and availability rules.

sections.title: JavaScript Values and Expressions
sections.summary: Use the core building blocks of JavaScript to represent and transform event information.

topics.title: JavaScript Values and First Expressions
topics.summary: Evaluate strings, numbers, booleans, null, and undefined and observe how expressions produce new values.
learningGoals: Recognize JavaScript's common primitive values.
Explain the difference between a value and an expression.
Use typeof carefully to inspect values.

topics.title: Variables with const and let
topics.summary: Name event information clearly and choose const or let based on whether a binding must change.
learningGoals: Declare variables with const and let.
Choose clear camelCase names.
Update a let binding without confusing reassignment with mutation.

topics.title: Strings, Numbers, and Template Literals
topics.summary: Format event details with string operations, arithmetic, and readable template literals.
learningGoals: Combine strings without accidental numeric coercion.
Perform basic arithmetic for capacity and availability.
Interpolate values into template literals.

topics.title: Comparisons, Conditionals, and Logic
topics.summary: Use strict comparisons, logical operators, and conditional branches to decide what an interface should say.
learningGoals: Compare values with strict equality and relational operators.
Combine boolean conditions with logical operators.
Choose between if, else if, and else branches.

sections.title: Module Project
sections.summary: Apply values, formatting, comparisons, and conditions in one focused event-message project.

topics.title: Build an Event Announcement Generator
topics.summary: Create announcement text that changes with event location, capacity, and registration availability.
learningGoals: Represent an event with clearly named values.
Compute remaining capacity.
Generate an appropriate registration message with conditionals.

projectBrief.scenario: A campus activities office needs a small JavaScript program that turns event facts into one clear registration announcement.
projectBrief.role: Beginner JavaScript developer responsible for the announcement data and decision logic.
projectBrief.workspace: A browser JavaScript workspace with script.js and Console output. No framework, package installation, backend, or external network is required.
projectBrief.deliverable: An Event Announcement Generator that stores event data, calculates remaining seats, decides registration status, builds one readable message, and outputs the finished announcement.
requirements: Use only JavaScript values, variables, operators, boolean logic, conditionals, template literals, and Console output taught in Module 1.
Build the project cumulatively so every step begins with the complete previous solution.
Add one clear responsibility per step and preserve all previously completed behavior.
Avoid temporary progress logs that later steps must delete.
Produce one final announcement output at the end of the project.

stepLadder.title: Store the event identity
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The campus announcement cannot describe an event until the program knows which event it is talking about and where it takes place. Task: Create only `eventName` and `location` as constants.

stepLadder.title: Store registration numbers
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The announcement will eventually tell students whether space is available, but the program first needs the total capacity and current registration count. Task: Keep the complete Step 1 code and add only `capacity` and `registered` as number constants.

stepLadder.title: Calculate remaining seats
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Raw capacity and registration counts do not directly tell a student how many seats are still open. Task: Keep all previous values and add only `seatsRemaining = capacity - registered`.

stepLadder.title: Store the deadline state
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Available seats alone are not enough to decide whether registration is open because the signup deadline may already have passed. Task: Keep the complete previous solution and add only the boolean `deadlinePassed`.

stepLadder.title: Calculate whether registration is open
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The program now knows seat availability and deadline state, but it still needs one clear rule for whether a student may register. Task: Add only `isOpen` so registration is open when seats remain and the deadline has not passed.

stepLadder.title: Choose the status text
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The boolean `isOpen` is useful to code, but students need a readable registration message. Task: Keep the complete availability rule and add `statusText` with one `if/else` that assigns `Registration open` or `Registration closed`.

stepLadder.title: Build the final announcement
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The project now has all of the facts and decisions, but they are still separate values instead of one announcement a student can read. Task: Add only the `announcement` template literal using the event name, location, status text, and remaining seats.

stepLadder.title: Show the finished announcement
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The announcement is complete in memory, but nobody can see it until the program outputs it. Task: Keep the entire working project and add only `console.log(announcement)`.

modules.title: Collections, Repetition, and Functions
modules.purpose: Help learners organize related data, name reusable operations, and process collections with clear iteration patterns before moving into browser interaction.
learningObjectives: Create arrays, read indexed values, inspect length, and append items with push.
Model structured records with objects and combine objects inside arrays.
Define reusable functions with parameters and return values.
Use for...of, map, and filter to process collections.
Combine collections and functions in a cumulative Event List Planner.
guidedExercises: Model several campus events with arrays and objects.
Trace iteration one element at a time.
Extract repeated formatting and filtering behavior into functions.
modules.moduleProject: Build an Event List Planner that filters and formats structured event records with reusable functions.

sections.title: Collections, Functions, and Iteration
sections.summary: Organize data with arrays and objects, name reusable work with functions, then process collections with for...of, map, and filter.

topics.title: Arrays and Indexed Data
topics.summary: Store ordered values together, read items by position, and grow a collection with push.
learningGoals: Create arrays that hold related values in order.
Read array items by index and distinguish index from length.
Append a new value with push.

topics.title: Objects and Event Records
topics.summary: Group related facts into objects, read and update properties, and combine objects inside arrays.
learningGoals: Create object records with named properties.
Read and update properties with dot notation.
Use arrays of objects as a collection of structured records.

topics.title: Functions, Parameters, and Return Values
topics.summary: Name reusable work, pass values through parameters, and return results to the caller.
learningGoals: Define and call reusable functions.
Use parameters to receive different input values.
Return a result that other code can store and reuse.

topics.title: Loops and Array Iteration
topics.summary: Visit every array item with for...of, transform items with map, and keep matching items with filter.
learningGoals: Use for...of to visit every value in an array.
Use map with a callback to transform every item.
Use filter with a boolean callback to keep matching items.

sections.title: Module Project
sections.summary: Combine arrays, objects, iteration, and functions in an event-planning program.

topics.title: Build an Event List Planner
topics.summary: Filter a collection of event records and format a useful schedule with reusable functions.
learningGoals: Model multiple events with an array of objects.
Filter events by a learner-selected criterion.
Format selected events through a reusable function.

projectBrief.scenario: A campus programs team needs a small JavaScript planner that selects Technology events and turns them into readable schedule lines.
projectBrief.role: Beginner JavaScript developer responsible for the event collection and reusable data-processing functions.
projectBrief.workspace: A browser JavaScript workspace with script.js and Console output. No framework, package installation, backend, or external network is required.
projectBrief.deliverable: An Event List Planner that stores event objects, uses focused predicate and formatting functions, filters and maps the collection, and outputs the selected schedule.
requirements: Use only arrays, objects, functions, filter, map, for...of, template literals, and Console output taught in Module 2.
Build the project cumulatively so every step begins with the complete previous solution.
Add one clear responsibility per step and preserve all previously completed behavior.
Keep source data, filtering, formatting, and final output as focused responsibilities.

stepLadder.title: Start the event collection
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The event planner cannot process a schedule until each event is represented as one structured record. Task: Create `events` as an array containing one event object with `name`, `category`, and `location`.

stepLadder.title: Complete the schedule data
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: One event is not enough to test a real planner, especially filtering across different categories. Task: Keep the first event and add three more event objects with the same `name`, `category`, and `location` shape.

stepLadder.title: Identify Technology events
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The planner will need to select only Technology events, so it first needs one reusable yes-or-no rule for a single event. Task: Keep the complete event array and add only `isTechnology(event)` returning whether the category equals `Technology`.

stepLadder.title: Format one event
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Event objects are useful for code, but a student reading a schedule needs a short line with the event name and location. Task: Keep the data and predicate and add only `formatEvent(event)` returning `name — location`.

stepLadder.title: Select Technology events
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The planner still contains every category, but this schedule should include only Technology events. Task: Keep every previous function and add only `selectedEvents = events.filter(isTechnology)`.

stepLadder.title: Format the selected schedule
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The planner has selected the correct Technology event objects, but raw objects are not readable schedule lines for a student. Task: Keep the selected event array and add only `scheduleLines = selectedEvents.map(formatEvent)`.

stepLadder.title: Show every schedule line
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The schedule lines are ready in memory, but the planner has not shown them anywhere yet. Task: Keep the complete data pipeline and add only a `for...of` loop that logs every line in `scheduleLines`.

modules.title: Browser Interaction and Data
modules.purpose: Connect JavaScript to browser behavior, user input, local JSON data, async control flow, and explicit interface states.
learningObjectives: Select, update, create, and append DOM elements.
Respond to clicks, form submissions, and changed controls.
Parse JSON and check broad data shape at boundaries.
Use Promises, async/await, and try/catch.
Fetch local JSON and check response.ok before parsing.
Represent loading, empty, success, and error states explicitly.
Build an Interactive Event Browser with one category filter.
guidedExercises: Render one event card from an object before rendering a collection.
Connect a filter control to a render function.
Trace promise states before using async-await.
Use a local events.json fixture so fetch behavior remains deterministic.
modules.moduleProject: Build an Interactive Event Browser that loads local data and supports filtering with resilient interface feedback.

sections.title: DOM, Events, and Async Data
sections.summary: Connect JavaScript to the page, respond to input, then load and validate local data asynchronously.

topics.title: Select and Update the DOM
topics.summary: Connect JavaScript to the page by selecting elements, changing text, and creating new elements safely.
learningGoals: Select elements with querySelector and querySelectorAll.
Update textContent and relevant attributes.
Render repeated event records without mixing data decisions into markup unnecessarily.

topics.title: Events, Forms, and User Input
topics.summary: Respond to clicks, handle form submission without reloading, and read values from form controls.
learningGoals: Register event listeners with named callbacks.
Read values from form controls.
Update rendered results after a user interaction.

topics.title: JSON and Data Boundaries
topics.summary: Distinguish JSON text from JavaScript values, parse incoming text, and check the broad shape of parsed data.
learningGoals: Distinguish JSON text from JavaScript objects and arrays.
Parse valid JSON with JSON.parse.
Serialize supported JavaScript data with JSON.stringify.

topics.title: Promises and async-await
topics.summary: Understand a Promise as a future result, use await inside async functions, and handle rejected work with try/catch.
learningGoals: Describe the states of a promise.
Use await only inside an async function.
Handle rejected asynchronous work with try and catch.

topics.title: Fetch Local Event Data
topics.summary: Load a local JSON file with fetch, check the HTTP response, and parse its body into JavaScript data.
learningGoals: Fetch a local JSON file without external network access.
Check response.ok before decoding a response body.
Await response.json and render the resulting event array.

topics.title: Loading, Error, Empty, and Success States
topics.summary: Represent asynchronous UI states explicitly so the learner always knows whether data is loading, failed, empty, or ready.
learningGoals: Show a loading state before awaiting data.
Present useful error feedback after a failed request or parse.
Distinguish an empty result from an error.
Render success content and accessible status messages.

sections.title: Module Project
sections.summary: Combine DOM rendering, local JSON loading, explicit UI states, and one category filter.

topics.title: Build an Interactive Event Browser
topics.summary: Build a browser app that renders local event data, communicates async states, and filters events by one category.
learningGoals: Load local JSON data with async-await and fetch.
Render and filter event records in response to user input.
Keep loading, error, empty, and success states mutually understandable.

projectBrief.scenario: A campus engagement page needs a small browser application that loads local event data, renders it, and lets students filter the visible events.
projectBrief.role: Beginner frontend JavaScript developer responsible for DOM rendering, local data loading, visible states, and category interaction.
projectBrief.workspace: A cumulative browser-web workspace with index.html, script.js, and a local data/events.json fixture. No framework, backend, package installation, or external network is required.
projectBrief.deliverable: An Interactive Event Browser that renders event records, loads local JSON safely, communicates loading/error/empty/success outcomes, and filters the visible list by category.
requirements: Use browser DOM, form/control events, for...of, filter, async/await, fetch, response.ok, and response.json patterns taught in Module 3.
Keep the JSON fixture local so the project works without external network access.
Build the project cumulatively so every step begins with the complete previous solution.
Add one clear responsibility per step and preserve all previously completed behavior.
Do not use temporary preview records that later steps must remove.
Make observable states and alternate branches explicit in each step's expected result.

stepLadder.title: Select the event list
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The event browser will eventually render event records, but JavaScript first needs a reference to the list already provided by the page. Task: Select only `#event-list` and store it in `eventList`.

stepLadder.title: Render an event array
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Loaded event objects cannot help a student until the browser can turn them into visible list items. Task: Keep `eventList` and add only `renderEvents(events)`: clear the list, loop with `for...of`, create one `li` per event, set `name - location`, and append it.

stepLadder.title: Select the status element
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Loading, empty, success, and error states need one visible place where the browser can explain what is happening. Task: Keep the complete renderer and select only `#status` into `status`.

stepLadder.title: Add event state
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Filtering later will require the browser to remember the complete loaded event list instead of losing the source records after rendering. Task: Keep all DOM references and the renderer and add only `let allEvents = []`.

stepLadder.title: Show the loading state
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Loading local data is asynchronous, so the page should immediately tell the learner that work has started instead of appearing frozen. Task: Keep everything from Step 4 and add and call `loadEvents()` with one responsibility: set the status to `Loading events...`.

stepLadder.title: Request the local event data
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The browser currently has no event records to render because the data lives in a local JSON file. Task: Keep the visible loading behavior and update only `loadEvents()` to await `fetch("./data/events.json")` into `response`.

stepLadder.title: Reject a failed response
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: `fetch` can return a Response even when the local request failed, so decoding blindly could treat an error response as valid event data. Task: Keep the local request and add only the `response.ok` guard, throwing `Could not load events` when false.

stepLadder.title: Decode and count the events
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The browser has a successful Response object, but the renderer needs JavaScript event records rather than the raw response body. Task: Keep the request and response check, decode JSON into `allEvents`, then show the loaded count.

stepLadder.title: Render the loaded events
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The event records are now loaded into memory, but students still cannot see them on the page. Task: Keep the complete load flow and add only `renderEvents(allEvents)` after the successful decode/count.

stepLadder.title: Handle an empty event file
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: A successful JSON request may contain zero events, and a blank list with no explanation would look broken. Task: Keep the successful load and rendering behavior and add only the zero-length branch: show `No events found`, render an empty list, and return.

stepLadder.title: Handle loading errors
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Network or data-loading failures should not leave the browser stuck on `Loading events...` with no explanation. Task: Keep the complete success and empty behavior and wrap only the load path in `try...catch`; in `catch`, clear the list and show `Could not load events`.

stepLadder.title: Select the category control
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The event browser has loaded all events, but it cannot react to a category choice until JavaScript has a reference to the existing filter control. Task: Keep the fully working loader and select only `#category-filter` into `categoryFilter`.

stepLadder.title: Derive events for one category
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The app must show one category without destroying the complete event list that future filter choices still need. Task: Keep the loaded source data and add only `eventsForCategory(category)`: return all events for `All`, otherwise return the matching subset.

stepLadder.title: Show one category view
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: A filtered array by itself is not useful to the learner until the browser renders it and explains whether anything matched. Task: Keep every previous feature and add only `showCategory(category)`: derive visible events, render them, then show `No matching events` or the visible count.

stepLadder.title: Update the view when the category changes
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The category-view logic is complete, but changing the select control still does nothing because no event connects the user's choice to that logic. Task: Keep the complete application, add `handleCategoryChange(event)` so it calls `showCategory(event.currentTarget.value)`, then attach it to the filter's `change` event.

modules.title: Final Capstone: Campus Event Explorer
modules.purpose: Transfer the complete JavaScript Foundations skill set into one progressive, data-driven browser application.
learningObjectives: Model, load, filter, and render campus event data.
Organize behavior into focused functions with explicit inputs and outputs.
Respond to user controls with clear and accessible interface updates.
Handle loading, error, empty, and success states deliberately.
guidedExercises: Work through the capstone milestones in order in one cumulative browser workspace.
Check keyboard interaction and status messaging after each major interface change.
Run cumulative source checks after each milestone.

sections.title: Final Capstone
sections.summary: Build one progressive Campus Event Explorer that loads local data, supports discovery controls, and communicates every interface state.

topics.title: Campus Event Explorer
topics.summary: Build a complete browser application for discovering campus events from a local JSON data source.
learningGoals: Load and validate local campus event data.
Render useful event cards from structured records.
Filter events through accessible controls.
Communicate loading, error, empty, and success states.
Refactor repeated behavior into focused functions and verify the complete application.

projectBrief.scenario: A campus engagement office needs a small browser application that helps students discover upcoming events without depending on an external service.
projectBrief.role: Beginner frontend developer responsible for the application's JavaScript behavior and data flow.
projectBrief.workspace: A cumulative browser-web workspace with semantic starter HTML, a small stylesheet, script.js, and a local events.json fixture. No terminal, package installation, framework, backend, or external network is required.
projectBrief.deliverable: A Campus Event Explorer that loads local event data, renders accessible event cards, supports useful filtering, and presents clear loading, error, empty, and success states.
requirements: Use JavaScript language and browser APIs taught in this course; do not introduce a framework or build tool.
Keep events.json local so the project works without external network access.
Separate data loading, filtering, and rendering into focused functions.
Use event listeners for learner controls and avoid inline JavaScript handlers.
Check response.ok and handle rejected or invalid data paths.
Provide distinguishable loading, error, empty, and success states.
Keep status feedback understandable to keyboard and assistive-technology users.
Use the browser preview and cumulative source checks; do not require Judge0 or terminal execution.

stepLadder.title: Format one event
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Each event card needs one concise line that helps students understand the category, location, and seat availability without reading raw object fields. Task: Complete only `formatEventMeta(event)` and return one string containing those three values.

stepLadder.title: Build one event card
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The explorer has formatted event details, but it still needs a reusable DOM structure for showing one event consistently. Task: Keep the formatter and add only `createEventCard(event)`. Create an `article`, `h2`, and `p`, fill them with `textContent`, append the heading and metadata, and return the article.

stepLadder.title: Select the events section
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Reusable event cards cannot appear until JavaScript knows which page section should contain them. Task: Select `#events` and store it in `eventsElement`.

stepLadder.title: Render an event list
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The explorer can build one card, but students need the whole event array rendered as a visible list of cards. Task: Keep every previous function and add only `renderEvents(events)`: clear the events section, loop with `for...of`, and append one card for each event.

stepLadder.title: Add application state
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Filtering must always start from the complete loaded event list, so the app needs one stable place to remember that source data. Task: Add only `let allEvents = []`.

stepLadder.title: Filter by category
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Students need to narrow the explorer by category without deleting the original loaded records. Task: Add only `filterEvents(category)`. Return every event when the category is `all`; otherwise return only matching events.

stepLadder.title: Select the filter controls
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The filter logic exists, but the app cannot read the learner's category choice until JavaScript has references to the form and select elements. Task: Select `#filters` and `#category` into `filtersForm` and `categorySelect`.

stepLadder.title: Apply the filter on submit
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Choosing a category still does nothing because the form submission is not connected to the existing filter and renderer. Task: Add one `submit` listener to `filtersForm`, prevent the page reload, read `categorySelect.value`, filter `allEvents`, and render the visible events.

stepLadder.title: Request the local JSON file
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The explorer currently has no real event records because its data lives in the workspace's local `events.json` file. Task: Add only `fetchEvents()` with one `await fetch("./events.json")` call, then return the Response.

stepLadder.title: Reject failed responses
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: A completed fetch is not proof that the event file loaded successfully, so the app must reject failed responses before treating them as data. Task: Keep the local request and add only the `response.ok` guard, throwing `Could not load events` when false.

stepLadder.title: Decode the JSON body
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: A successful Response object still is not the event array that the rest of the explorer needs. Task: Update only `fetchEvents()`: await `response.json()`, store the decoded value in `records`, and return it.

stepLadder.title: Validate the data boundary
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Valid JSON can still have the wrong shape, and the renderer expects an array of events rather than an arbitrary object or value. Task: Update only `fetchEvents()` to verify `records` with `Array.isArray(records)` and throw if it is not an array.

stepLadder.title: Show a ready status
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Before loading begins, the explorer should tell the learner that it is ready rather than leaving the status area blank. Task: Keep everything from the previous step, select `#status`, add `showStatus(message)` using `textContent`, then call it with `Ready to load events.`.

stepLadder.title: Start in the loading state
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: Once startup begins, the explorer should immediately show that data is being loaded so the page does not appear unresponsive. Task: Keep the complete project and add and call `start()` with one responsibility: change the status to `Loading events…`. Do not fetch data yet.

stepLadder.title: Load the event data
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The loading state is visible, but the application still has no event records in its state. Task: Keep every function and listener, update only `start()` so it awaits `fetchEvents()`, stores the returned array in `allEvents`, and reports the count.

stepLadder.title: Render the loaded events
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: The explorer now knows there are three events, but students still cannot see the actual events. Task: Keep the entire working project and add only `renderEvents(allEvents)` after the successful load.

stepLadder.title: Handle an empty event list
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: A valid event file can contain zero records, and leaving the card area blank would make the explorer look broken. Task: Keep every previous feature and add only the empty-array branch inside `start()`: show `No events found.`, render an empty list, and return.

stepLadder.title: Handle loading errors
stepLadder.requirement: Problem: A request or data-validation failure should not leave the explorer stuck on a loading message with no explanation. Task: Keep the complete application and wrap only the startup load path in `try...catch`, showing `Could not load events.` in `catch`.

assessmentAndDelivery.suggestedBeginnerRhythm: One module per week or two short topics per study session.
recommendedCourseDeliverables: One progressive Campus Event Explorer capstone
assessmentAndDelivery.closingNote: Learners finish able to build beginner browser applications with interaction, local asynchronous data, and resilient interface states.

authoringGuidance: This course uses profileId web, workspaceProfileId browser-web-runner, and workspacePolicyId javascript-browser-workspace.
Hands-on JavaScript tasks use kind code_input, fixedLanguage web, recipeType source_checks, and local browser workspace files.
Every code_input must include explicit sourceChecks and must not include stdout tests.
Use local events.json fixtures for fetch practice because the browser workspace does not provide external network access.
Teach visible behavior and state transitions in the browser preview; do not tell learners to use a terminal or Judge0.
Keep JavaScript Foundations framework-free and package-free.
Teach JSON, promises and async-await, local fetch, and loading, error, empty, and success states before the capstone.
Topic and section counts are pedagogy-driven for this course; do not generalize them into fixed curriculum cardinality rules.
